lead: Rankings, growth narratives and policy arguments all depend on what the source actually measures. Today’s opening coverage separates conditional forecasts, reported approvals and paper values from completed outcomes.

sections.title: What a forecast or ranking actually establishes
sections.intro: A sparse ranking interface and a conditional superintelligence essay require different checks.

sections.title: Reporting to authorities needs context
sections.intro: A secondhand account, an inaccessible court report and a leadership excerpt do not establish universal legal rules.

sections.title: Usage growth has a cost side
sections.intro: Agent-created issues, trial abuse and missing demand arguments measure different parts of product economics.

sections.title: Approvals, hiring and demonstrations are different stages
sections.intro: Chip licensing, a reported development role and a console interface do not prove deployment outcomes.

sections.title: Paper gains and negotiating prices remain conditional
sections.intro: Estimated stakes and acquisition talks are not cash distributions or completed deals.
